subject: Oceanography
title: Sewage and Pathogens
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sewage and Pathogens.

hook.text: 80% of wastewater worldwide enters the ocean untreated—carrying pathogens, drugs, and chemicals.

buildup.text: Raw sewage introduces bacteria, viruses, and parasites—contaminating shellfish and swimming beaches.

discovery.text: Pharmaceutical residues pass through treatment plants—hormones and antibiotics are found in coastal waters.

twist.text: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria evolve in sewage-polluted waters—the ocean may become a breeding ground for superbugs.

climax.text: Coral reefs near sewage outfalls suffer double the disease rates—pathogens weaken already stressed colonies.

punchline.text: What flows down the drain eventually flows into the sea.

quiz.question: How much of global wastewater enters the ocean untreated?
